questions.chapter: Chapter 1: Continuous & Discrete-Time Signals and Systems
questions.text: Explain Signal Classifications: Continuous-Time (CT) vs Discrete-Time (DT), Periodic vs Aperiodic, Even vs Odd, Energy vs Power signals ($E = \int_{-\infty}^\infty |x(t)|^2 dt, P = \lim_{T \to \infty} \frac{1}{T} \int_{-T/2}^{T/2} |x(t)|^2 dt$). Explain Unit Step, Unit Impulse, and Unit Ramp functions.

questions.chapter: Chapter 1: Continuous & Discrete-Time Signals and Systems
questions.text: Explain System Properties: Linearity (Superposition), Time-Invariance, Causality, Stability (BIBO Stability $\int |h(t)| dt < \infty$), Memory (Static vs Dynamic), and Invertibility. Test these properties for $y(t) = t x(t)$ and $y[n] = x[2n]$.

questions.chapter: Chapter 2: Linear Time-Invariant Systems, Convolution Integral & Convolution Sum
questions.text: Explain Linear Time-Invariant (LTI) Systems and Impulse Response ($h(t)$). Derive Convolution Integral ($y(t) = x(t) * h(t) = \int_{-\infty}^\infty x(\tau) h(t - \tau) d\tau$) and Convolution Sum. Evaluate convolution of two rectangular pulses graphically and analytically.

questions.chapter: Chapter 3: Continuous-Time Fourier Series & Continuous-Time Fourier Transform
questions.text: Explain Continuous-Time Fourier Series (CTFS: Trigonometric and Exponential forms). State Dirichlet's conditions. Find exponential Fourier series coefficients for a periodic square wave.

questions.chapter: Chapter 3: Continuous-Time Fourier Series & Continuous-Time Fourier Transform
questions.text: Explain Continuous-Time Fourier Transform (CTFT) and Inverse CTFT. State and prove CTFT Properties: Linearity, Time Shifting, Frequency Shifting (Modulation), Time Scaling, Duality, Differentiation, and Parseval's Energy Theorem.

questions.chapter: Chapter 6: Z-Transform, ROC Properties, Inverse Z-Transform & Discrete System Analysis
questions.text: Explain Laplace Transform and Region of Convergence (ROC). State properties of ROC. Find Laplace Transform and ROC of $x(t) = e^{-at} u(t) - e^{-bt} u(-t)$. Explain transfer function $H(s) = \frac{Y(s)}{X(s)}$ and pole-zero plot for system stability and causality.
